text: MongoDB issue SERVER-130130 reports that recipient-side orphan bookkeeping can drift below the true count when a migration delete entry matches no recipient document. Jira lists the issue as unresolved for affected 6.0.0, 7.0.0, and 8.0.0 versions; it describes a bookkeeping defect, not direct user-data loss. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13)

Range deletion follows the ownership metadata handoff asynchronously. MongoDB waits for relevant open cursors before deleting the source copy, and the balancer can start a later range migration while an earlier delete phase is still pending. Open cursors can delay cleanup, and large range deletions can cause cache and I/O stress. Current MongoDB documentation says cleanup is resilient to a replica-set primary crash or restart. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

The current MongoDB manual marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated starting in 8.0. The command runs on a shard primary, waits for orphan cleanup across the namespace, and does not directly start deletion; it must not run on mongos. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Range cleanup can wait on open cursors: the current balancer procedure deletes the source copy only after open cursors on the range are gone. A MongoDB 3.4 forum response explains that an already-being-processed-for-deletion response typically means a query still holds a cursor; the response alone does not establish a failure. (medium confidence)

The MongoDB 9.0 manual marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated since 8.0 and says it waits for all orphaned documents in the namespace to be cleaned from a majority of the shard's replica-set members; it does not delete them directly. Alibaba's 2026 upgrade guide says MongoDB 4.4 introduced automatic migration recovery and that cleanupOrphaned can verify the background cleanup. Apply version-specific guidance before using older cleanup loops. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

A range migration updates ownership metadata before the source shard deletes its old copy; the balancer deletes that copy after no open cursors remain. These leftover source copies are orphaned documents and consume disk while range deletion is pending. (high confidence)

MongoDB 8.2 documentation sets orphanCleanupDelaySecs to 3600 seconds by default and terminateSecondaryReadsOnOrphanCleanup to true. The source shard waits for existing primary reads and then the delay before deleting orphans; secondaries terminate reads that began before migration commit. If that termination setting is disabled, a secondary read may silently miss moved documents; long-running reads may otherwise receive QueryPlanKilled and need to resume. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

One MongoDB 3.4 operator reported cleanupOrphaned running for three days across more than 100 shards, with rangeDeleter logs often showing zero deletions. This is a single 2018 report, not an expected duration for current versions. (low confidence)

MongoDB issue SERVER-78703 documents a historical count behavior where numOrphans stayed at its pre-deletion value until range deletion finished, so the tracked count could exceed the remaining documents during cleanup. The issue lists fixes in 7.0.0-rc7 and 7.1.0-rc0. (low confidence)

MongoDB defines orphaned documents as documents on a shard that also exist in chunks on other shards. They can remain on a former donor while range cleanup is incomplete after ownership moves. (high confidence)

Starting in MongoDB 8.2, long-running secondary reads can be terminated before orphan deletion to avoid missing documents; the default orphanCleanupDelaySecs also increased from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds. Applications with long-running secondary reads should account for version-specific termination behavior during chunk migrations. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
